seo.title: Berlin's Vegan Food Scene (2026) | tabiji.ai
seo.metaDescription: Discover the 12 best vegan restaurants in Berlin for 2026. From zero-waste fine dining to classic street food and donuts, explore top plant-based eateries in Mitte, Prenzlauer Berg, and more. Your ultimate guide to Berlin's vibrant vegan culinary scene.

hero.subtitle: Berlin stands as a global vegan capital, boasting an incredible array of plant-based eateries, from innovative fine dining to delicious street food and cozy cafes, catering to every taste and budget.

picks.name: Kopps
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Kopps offers a sophisticated take on traditional German cuisine, completely re-imagined as plant-based. Known for its elegant ambiance and innovative seasonal menus, it's perfect for a special occasion or an elevated dining experience. They focus on fresh, regional ingredients.
picks.whatToOrder: The tasting menu for a full culinary journey, or their seasonal "Königsberger Klopse" if available.
picks.insiderTip: Book well in advance, especially for weekend dinner. Their weekend brunch is also exceptional and highly popular.
picks.redditQuote: "Kopps absolutely blew my mind last time I was in Berlin. Who knew vegan German food could be this good? Definitely worth the splurge!"

picks.name: Frea
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Frea pioneers a zero-waste philosophy in fine dining, creating exquisite vegan dishes with ingredients sourced directly from local farmers, often processing them entirely in-house. Their commitment to sustainability is matched only by the creativity and flavor of their tasting menus.
picks.whatToOrder: The evening tasting menu (their only option), which changes daily based on available produce.
picks.insiderTip: Reserve your table far ahead. Ask for a tour of their "compost room" to truly appreciate their zero-waste commitment.
picks.redditQuote: "Frea is more than just a meal, it's an experience. The zero-waste concept isn't a gimmick; the food is genuinely outstanding. Felt good supporting them."

picks.name: Ryong
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Ryong serves up incredibly flavorful and creative vegan Vietnamese-inspired dishes in a vibrant, casual setting. Known for their delicious bao burgers, crispy rice dishes, and unique starters, it's a bustling spot perfect for a quick, satisfying meal with friends.
picks.whatToOrder: The "The Crazy Crispy" (crispy rice, tofu, peanut sauce) or any of their signature Bao Burgers.
picks.insiderTip: It can get very busy, especially during lunch and dinner rushes. Be prepared for a short wait or try to visit during off-peak hours.
picks.redditQuote: "Ryong is my go-to for delicious vegan Asian food in Berlin. That Crazy Crispy dish is addictive, and their bao buns are next level!"

picks.name: Brammibal's Donuts
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Brammibal's is a Berlin institution, offering an astonishing variety of gourmet vegan donuts. From classic glazed to adventurous seasonal flavors, their donuts are fluffy, indulgent, and pair perfectly with their specialty coffee. A perfect treat any time of day.
picks.whatToOrder: Their classic "Maple Smoked Coconut Bacon" donut or a seasonal fruit-filled option.
picks.insiderTip: They often sell out of popular flavors, especially later in the day. Go early for the best selection!
picks.redditQuote: "Seriously, Brammibal's donuts are insane. You'd never guess they're vegan. The maple bacon is a game changer!"

picks.name: Vöner
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Vöner is Berlin's answer to the iconic Döner Kebab, but entirely vegan. They craft delicious, hearty plant-based Döner, Currywurst, and Schnitzel sandwiches that perfectly capture the essence of German street food, making it a must-try for locals and tourists alike.
picks.whatToOrder: The classic "Vöner Teller" with their signature sauce, or a "Vöner im Brot."
picks.insiderTip: This is a cash-only establishment, so make sure you have some Euros on hand. It's a small place, best for a quick bite or takeaway.
picks.redditQuote: "Vöner is the real deal. Missing Döner after going vegan? This place scratches that itch perfectly. So good, especially late at night."

picks.name: The Bowl
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Located in the vibrant RAW Gelände, The Bowl specializes in nourishing, plant-based 'clean eating' dishes, primarily served in creative and colorful bowls. With an emphasis on fresh, often raw ingredients, it's a perfect spot for a healthy, delicious meal in a trendy setting.
picks.whatToOrder: The "Happy Bowl" for a well-rounded and satisfying meal, or their famous raw cheesecake for dessert.
picks.insiderTip: Combine your visit with exploring the RAW Gelände's street art, clubs, and markets, especially on weekends.
picks.redditQuote: "Love The Bowl for a healthy reset. Everything is so fresh and beautifully presented. Their raw cheesecakes are dangerously good!"

picks.name: Cookies Cream
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Hidden down a back alley, Cookies Cream is a renowned vegetarian fine dining restaurant with an extensive vegan menu. It offers an innovative culinary journey focused on seasonal vegetables, presented with artistry and precision in a chic, industrial-glam setting.
picks.whatToOrder: Ask for the dedicated vegan tasting menu, or try their signature "Parmesan Dumplings" (vegan version available).
picks.insiderTip: Finding the entrance can be tricky – look for the unmarked door next to the Westin Grand Hotel's delivery entrance. Definitely make a reservation.
picks.redditQuote: "Cookies Cream is a Berlin institution for a reason. Even as a meat-eater, I was blown away by their vegan dishes. The atmosphere is super cool too."

picks.name: Alaska Bar
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Alaska Bar brings a slice of vegan Spain to Berlin with its delightful array of plant-based tapas. This cozy, lively spot in Neukölln is perfect for sharing small plates, enjoying creative cocktails, and soaking in a relaxed, friendly atmosphere.
picks.whatToOrder: The "Patatas Bravas," "Croquetas," and their rotating seasonal specials.
picks.insiderTip: It's a popular evening spot, so arrive early if you want a table, especially on weekends. Their cocktail menu is also worth exploring.
picks.redditQuote: "Alaska Bar in Neukölln has the best vegan tapas! Everything is so flavorful, and it's such a cute place for a date or drinks with friends."

picks.name: Lia's Kitchen
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Lia's Kitchen is a beloved spot for hearty, satisfying vegan burgers and comfort food. With a focus on fresh ingredients and homemade sauces, their menu features classic burger options, creative toppings, and delicious sides like sweet potato fries and onion rings.
picks.whatToOrder: The "Classic Burger" with their homemade patty, or the "Chili Cheese Burger" for something more indulgent.
picks.insiderTip: They have a small outdoor seating area which is lovely on sunny days. Don't forget to check out their daily specials.
picks.redditQuote: "Lia's Kitchen makes a damn good vegan burger. The patties actually taste homemade, and their sweet potato fries are perfect."

picks.name: Sfizy Veg
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Sfizy Veg is Berlin's first entirely vegan Italian pizzeria, renowned for its authentic Neapolitan-style pizzas with delicious plant-based cheeses and creative toppings. It's a cozy, unpretentious spot that proves vegan pizza can be just as, if not more, satisfying than its traditional counterpart.
picks.whatToOrder: The "Pizza Funghi e Tartufo" (mushroom and truffle oil) or any of their seasonal specials.
picks.insiderTip: They offer gluten-free crusts upon request. It's a relatively small restaurant, so consider takeaway during peak hours.
picks.redditQuote: "Sfizy Veg has the best vegan pizza I've ever had, hands down. The crust is perfect, and the 'cheese' is surprisingly good. A must-try in Neukölln."

picks.name: Chaostheorie
picks.whyItMadeTheList: More than just a bar, Chaostheorie is a fully vegan cocktail bar offering a delicious menu of plant-based snacks and larger plates. It's known for its inventive cocktails, laid-back atmosphere, and being a perfect late-night spot to enjoy good food and drinks.
picks.whatToOrder: Their "Vöner Burger" or "Loaded Nachos" alongside one of their expertly crafted cocktails.
picks.insiderTip: It's a great spot for a relaxed evening out, especially if you're looking for good vegan food after most restaurants close.
picks.redditQuote: "Chaostheorie is my favorite chill bar in Friedrichshain. Great cocktails, and their vegan food is surprisingly good for a bar – those nachos hit different!"

picks.name: Swing Kitchen
picks.whyItMadeTheList: Originating from Austria, Swing Kitchen offers a modern take on classic American diner food, entirely vegan. With a menu featuring burgers, wraps, fries, and shakes, it's a popular choice for a quick, satisfying, and ethically conscious fast-food fix.
picks.whatToOrder: The "Vienna Burger" or their crispy "Crispy Chickin Burger" with a side of fries and a vegan milkshake.
picks.insiderTip: They have multiple locations across the city, making it a convenient option no matter where you are. The Ku'damm location is great for people-watching.
picks.redditQuote: "Swing Kitchen is my go-to when I need a quick vegan burger fix. It's reliably good, and their milkshakes are surprisingly creamy."

faq.question: Is Berlin really that vegan-friendly compared to other major cities?
faq.answer: Yes, Berlin is widely considered one of the most vegan-friendly cities in the world. It boasts an incredibly high concentration of fully vegan restaurants, cafes, and shops, often surpassing other major global capitals in terms of variety, innovation, and accessibility. You'll find plant-based options integrated into nearly every culinary category.

faq.question: What neighborhoods are best for finding vegan food in Berlin?
faq.answer: While vegan options are spread throughout the city, some neighborhoods are particularly dense with plant-based eateries. Mitte, Prenzlauer Berg, Friedrichshain, and Neukölln are excellent starting points, offering a wide range from upscale dining to casual cafes and street food. Exploring these areas will give you a taste of Berlin's diverse vegan scene.

faq.question: Are there vegan-friendly supermarkets or grocery stores in Berlin?
faq.answer: Absolutely! Berlin is home to several fully vegan supermarkets like Veganz, offering a vast selection of plant-based products, from specialty cheeses to ready-to-eat meals. Additionally, conventional supermarkets like Edeka, Rewe, and Lidl have extensive vegan sections, making it easy to find staples and unique items.

faq.question: Is it expensive to eat vegan in Berlin?
faq.answer: The cost of eating vegan in Berlin varies widely, just like with non-vegan options. You can find incredibly budget-friendly street food like Vöner for under €10, mid-range casual dining for €10-20 per person, and high-end fine dining experiences that can range from €50-80+. Overall, it's very accessible for all budgets.

faq.question: Can I find traditional German dishes made vegan in Berlin?
faq.answer: Yes, many traditional German dishes have been cleverly re-imagined as vegan in Berlin. You can find plant-based versions of Currywurst, Döner, Schnitzel, and even more refined dishes like Königsberger Klopse. Restaurants like Kopps specialize in elevating classic German flavors with a vegan twist.

faq.question: Do I need to book reservations for vegan restaurants in Berlin?
faq.answer: For most casual vegan eateries and street food spots, reservations are not necessary. However, for popular mid-range restaurants, and especially for fine dining establishments like Kopps, Frea, or Cookies Cream, making a reservation well in advance is highly recommended to secure a table, particularly on weekends.

methodology: Our selection of Berlin's best vegan venues for 2026 is based on extensive research, expert reviews, local recommendations, and consistent high ratings for quality, innovation, atmosphere, and service. We prioritized fully plant-based establishments offering diverse culinary experiences across various price points and neighborhoods.
